provenance: Written from working knowledge as a schema demonstration. Every identifier must be resolved against Orphanet, OMIM, MONDO and HPO before use. The `confidence` field marks which rows to check first.

definitions.source: EU Regulation 141/2000 on orphan medicinal products

ontologies.name: Mondo Disease Ontology
ontologies.role: the merge target — exists to unify the others

ontologies.name: Orphanet
ontologies.role: European rare-disease reference; prevalence and expert centres

ontologies.name: Human Phenotype Ontology
ontologies.role: the phenotype vocabulary that makes cases comparable

ontologies.name: ICD-11
ontologies.role: billing, mortality, health statistics; first ICD with real rare-disease coverage

ontologies.name: Genetic and Rare Diseases Information Center
Unified Medical Language System
ontologies.role: concept ids that bridge clinical terminologies

fieldFacts.claim: approximately 7 000-8 000 distinct rare diseases are catalogued
350-400 million people worldwide live with a rare disease
fieldFacts.verify: quoted directly in the Broad/CTG announcement, 2026-07-21

fieldFacts.claim: fewer than 1 in 20 rare diseases has an approved treatment
fieldFacts.verify: quoted directly in the Broad/CTG announcement, 2026-07-21

fieldFacts.claim: roughly 70-80% of rare diseases are genetic in origin
around half of patients referred for rare-disease diagnosis end without a molecular diagnosis
the diagnostic odyssey averages roughly 5 years

diseases.name: NF2-related schwannomatosis
diseases.note: Renamed in the 2022 consensus. The old name still dominates the corpus.

diseases.name: Duchenne muscular dystrophy
synonyms: デュシェンヌ型筋ジストロフィー
diseases.note: Exon-skipping and gene therapy approved for subsets; not curative.

diseases.name: Cystic fibrosis
diseases.note: The modifier-therapy success story rare disease is measured against.

diseases.name: Spinal muscular atrophy
diseases.mechanism: SMN protein deficiency; motor neuron loss
diseases.note: Three approved therapies; the proof that ultra-rare economics can work.

diseases.name: Zellweger spectrum disorder
diseases.note: Base editing repaired liver function in a mouse model (Broad, 2026).

diseases.name: Dravet syndrome
diseases.mechanism: Nav1.1 loss of function in interneurons
diseases.note: A rare genetic epilepsy of the class CTG's ARPA-H programme targets.

diseases.name: CDKL5 deficiency disorder
diseases.note: Gene known, mechanism not. The common ultra-rare situation.

diseases.name: Progressive myoclonic epilepsy, unsolved subgroup
diseases.note: A real clinical grouping with no ontology id, because it is defined by what was NOT found. Entries like this are invisible to any pipeline keyed on identifiers.

diseases.name: Undiagnosed multisystem syndrome (UDN-style)
diseases.note: The Undiagnosed Diseases Network's caseload. Not a disease entry — a placeholder for a patient the catalogue cannot name.

diseases.name: Fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva
diseases.note: Roughly one in two million. An ultra-rare disease with a solved mechanism.

diseases.name: Alkaptonuria
diseases.note: Garrod's original inborn error of metabolism, 1902.

diseases.name: Ultra-rare de novo variant syndrome, n<5 reported
diseases.note: The regime CTG is built for, and the regime where every statistic in this repository is at its limit: n = 1.
